I'm a Mechatronics Engineer and graduate of Assiut University, specializing in Industrial Artificial Intelligence and smart manufacturing applications. My work focuses on developing AI-driven solutions for predictive maintenance, fault diagnosis, anomaly detection, and Explainable AI (XAI) to support intelligent decision-making in industrial environments. During the SAPRS graduation project, my primary contribution was designing and developing the Industrial AI layer, integrating machine learning models, intelligent diagnostics, explainable AI, and backend AI services into a complete Industry 4.0 platform.

As a USAID Scholar since 2021 and an exchange student at Middle Tennessee State University (MTSU), I gained international academic experience, leadership training, and cross-cultural collaboration skills. Alongside my engineering education, I completed the Digital Egypt Pioneers Initiative (DEPI) in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, applying the acquired knowledge directly to the Industrial AI layer of my graduation project.

05 · Flagship Case Study

SAPRS — a PLC-controlled Industry 4.0 system with an Industrial AI layer.

Graduation project, Assiut University · Sep 2025 – Jul 2026 · Graded A-

The following sections describe the complete SAPRS multidisciplinary engineering system. My primary contribution focused on the Industrial AI layer, including predictive maintenance, machine learning, fault diagnosis, Explainable AI (XAI), backend AI integration, and intelligent decision support.

INDUSTRIAL AUTOMATION → PLC CONTROL → INDUSTRIAL AI → OPERATOR

A working manufacturing cell, not a simulation.

Siemens S7-1200 FastAPI + WebSockets Node-RED Scikit-learn
Summary Problem Mechanical Control PLC Layer Communication Backend Historian AI Pipeline Knowledge Base Explainable AI Copilot Dashboard Challenges Contributions Results Gallery Downloads

Executive Summary

SAPRS is a physical, PLC-controlled manufacturing cell that turns recycled plastic into hexagonal output tiles — engineered end-to-end, from the Siemens control logic on the shop floor to the Industrial AI layer that watches over it. It's the graduation project I built through mechanical integration, control engineering and the full software stack, treating reliable automation as the foundation and Industrial AI as the diagnostic layer built on top of it — not the other way around.

CategoryIndustry 4.0 / Predictive Maintenance
Control HardwareSiemens S7-1200
Engineering Env.TIA Portal
Telemetry BridgeNode-RED
BackendFastAPI (REST + WebSockets)
StorageSQLite Historian
AI LayerScikit-learn + rules engine
GradeA-

Industrial Problem

Manufacturing cells built on standalone PLC logic can control a machine safely, but on their own they can't explain why a fault happened, or predict one before it stops production.

Problem Statement

PLC-controlled machines generate raw fault codes and telemetry, but that data rarely reaches an operator as a clear, evidence-based explanation — leaving root-cause diagnosis manual and reactive, and preventive maintenance dependent on fixed schedules rather than actual machine condition.

Engineering Objectives

Combine reliable PLC control with real-time telemetry, a structured fault knowledge base, and an Industrial AI layer that predicts, diagnoses and explains machine health to the operator in plain language — without weakening the safety or determinism of the control layer underneath it.

Mechanical System

The physical cell: a heated barrel-and-hopper injection unit feeding a hexagonal mold, driven by motor and actuator control, producing recycled-plastic tiles on real hardware.

01 Hopper & Barrel Assembly

Recycled plastic feedstock is fed through a heated barrel assembly ahead of the injection stage, visible on the machine's upper section.

02 Injection & Mold Stage

A guided rod/plate assembly drives material into the hexagonal mold cavity behind the observation window, cycling under PLC-timed control.

03 Operator HMI Panel

A physical touchscreen HMI and hardware E-stop sit on the control face of the cell, giving the operator direct machine-level control independent of the software dashboard.

04 Output — Hexagonal Tiles

Finished hexagonal recycled-plastic tiles, produced directly by the cell, ready for inspection and stacking.

The cell — barrel, mold stage, HMI panel and hardware E-stop
Output — finished tiles straight off the cell

Automation & Control

The Siemens S7-1200 is the deterministic core of the cell — every safety interlock and motion command originates here, independent of anything running above it in software. Click a stage below.

Sensors & Actuators

Field-level motor current sensing, position feedback and pneumatic/electric actuation — the physical inputs and outputs the PLC reads and drives every scan cycle.

PLC Layer

Signals the S7-1200 logic reads and drives directly, forming the raw telemetry surface the rest of the system is built on.

I/O

Motor Current

Read continuously to detect abnormal load and to feed both control logic and the AI layer's sensor fusion.

I/O

Position States

Axis and mechanism position feedback, used for sequencing the injection and mold cycle.

I/O

Cycle Counters

Tracks completed production cycles, feeding both the dashboard's cycle count and maintenance-interval logic.

I/O

E-Stop Signals

Hardware emergency-stop state, wired with the highest priority in the control logic, independent of the software layers above it.

Industrial Communication

Real-time PLC-to-Node-RED communication, engineered via TIA Portal logic, for reliable telemetry acquisition without dropped signals.

Siemens S7-1200

Publishes live telemetry — motor current, position states, cycle counters and e-stop signals — every scan cycle.

Backend Architecture

A FastAPI service sits at the center of the software stack — ingesting telemetry, validating it against a formal data contract, and serving both the dashboard and the AI layer.

FastAPI Core

Orchestrates ingestion from Node-RED and serving to the dashboard and Copilot, exposing both REST endpoints and WebSocket channels.

Historian

A SQLite Historian gives the cell indexed, queryable memory — every telemetry event and AI decision is stored, not just displayed and discarded.

Industrial AI Pipeline

From a live sensor reading to a diagnosed, explained recommendation — the complete decision path the AI layer runs on every cycle.

FIG. 1 — Complete Industrial AI System Sequence
FIG. 2 — AI Decision Pipeline
01
Sensor Fusion

Telemetry channels are combined into a single feature set describing current machine state.

02
Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

A Scikit-learn model flags deviations from normal operating patterns without needing pre-labeled failure data.

03
Health Index Engine

Anomaly output feeds a digital-twin health score, giving a single at-a-glance machine health figure.

04
Decision & Evidence Engine

A rules-based engine cross-references live telemetry against the fault knowledge base for actionable, evidence-backed recommendations.

05
Explainable Output

Root cause, confidence and recommended actions are surfaced to the operator — through the dashboard and the AI Copilot.

Knowledge Base

A structured fault knowledge base mapping Siemens PLC fault codes to root-cause reasoning — the evidence the Decision & Evidence Engine reasons over.

saprs.local/dashboard/knowledge

Fault Knowledge Base

PurposeSearchable, filterable catalogue of Siemens PLC fault codes — PID_Compact and Motion Control — with severity and category, backing every AI decision with a documented reference.
BenefitGives operators a structured reference instead of a raw fault code, and gives the AI layer a defined evidence base to reason over rather than a black-box guess.
88 fault codes catalogued
Categories: PID_Compact · Motion Control
Severities: Critical · Warning
Some engineering fields — failure mechanism, physical meaning, industrial impact, difficulty, safety notes, required tools, best practices, preventive actions — are not yet tracked by the backend and display as "Not yet documented." Populating these is an active, ongoing part of the knowledge base build-out.

Explainable AI

The AI layer is designed to show its work — every recommendation traces back to specific evidence, not a single opaque confidence score.

Step 01

Evidence

Live telemetry is checked against the fault knowledge base and current Health Index — the raw evidence behind any decision.

Step 02

Reasoning

The rules-based Decision & Evidence Engine matches that evidence against known fault patterns and root causes.

Step 03

Explanation

The result is surfaced as root cause, confidence and recommended actions — in language an operator can act on, through the dashboard or the Copilot.

Industrial AI Copilot

A natural-language interface for operator queries — explaining the latest AI decision, machine health and recommended actions on demand.

saprs.local/dashboard/copilot

Explainable AI Copilot

PurposeLets an operator ask the system directly why it stopped, what the latest AI decision was, or what maintenance is recommended, instead of digging through raw logs.
BenefitTurns the Decision & Evidence Engine's output into a conversational, on-demand explanation — closing the loop between raw telemetry and an operator's actual question.
Why did machine stop? Explain latest AI decision. Show latest fault. Show recommendations. Machine health. Generate maintenance summary.

Engineering Challenges & Solutions

FIX Reliable PLC-to-application telemetry
Engineered real-time PLC-to-Node-RED communication via TIA Portal logic to reliably capture motor current, position states, cycle counters and e-stop signals without dropped telemetry.
FIX Turning raw fault codes into root-cause reasoning
Built a fault-diagnosis knowledge base mapping Siemens PLC fault codes (PID_Compact, Motion Control) to structured root-cause reasoning, paired with a rules-based Decision and Evidence Engine.
FIX Keeping the AI layer explainable, not a black box
Developed an Explainable AI Copilot that answers operator questions in natural language and shows the evidence behind each recommendation, rather than a single opaque score.
FIX Keeping the data contract consistent end-to-end
Authored a formal telemetry data contract standardizing validation across the PLC-to-AI-to-dashboard pipeline, with full Git-based version control.

My Contributions

SAPRS was a multidisciplinary team graduation project. My personal focus and contribution was the Industrial AI layer, described below.

  • Designed and developed the Industrial AI layer of the SAPRS Industry 4.0 platform, integrating it with the system's PLC-controlled architecture, from field telemetry to the operator dashboard.
  • Built the FastAPI backend — REST APIs and WebSockets — and the SQLite Historian for indexed analytics.
  • Developed the predictive-maintenance ML module (Scikit-learn, sensor fusion, unsupervised anomaly detection) and the Health Index Engine.
  • Built the 88-entry fault knowledge base and the rules-based AI Decision & Evidence Engine.
  • Developed the Explainable AI Copilot and authored the formal telemetry data contract governing the AI pipeline.
The team — Mechatronics & Robotics Engineering, Assiut University

Results & Future Improvements

Project Results

A functioning cell producing recycled-plastic output on real hardware, with live telemetry, a working predictive-maintenance model, an 88-entry fault knowledge base, and an explainable AI copilot operators can query directly — reviewed and graded A- by the department.

Future Improvements

Finishing the remaining knowledge-base fields (failure mechanism, safety notes, preventive actions), expanding the historian to a full time-series database, and training the predictive model on a larger production dataset as the cell accumulates more run-time.
